title: Nine representations, thirteen projections, thirty-one metrics
text: Prot Two Vec is a benchmark harness for protein sequence embeddings. This week it went from two representations to nine, from two projections to 13, and from 10 metrics to 31. This is sigh. The interesting part is not the breadth. It is that the release added three new ways to catch a result that is secretly measuring something else and then caught its own.

title: What it is — every method against every reducer
text: So, what is it? You hand it sequences with group labels. It runs every embedding method against every dimensionality reducer and scores all of them with the same metrics, so the comparison is actually like-for-like. Nine ways to turn a sequence into a vector, from counting amino acids to calling a protein language model. Six of the nine need no PyTorch at all.

title: The floor — what a projection carrying nothing scores
text: Here is the metric that sets the tone for the whole release. Neighborhood preservation asks what fraction of each point's true nearest neighbors survive the projection, but that number has a floor. Even a projection carrying no information keeps some neighbors by luck, K over N minus one of them. So, the release ships the chance-corrected version and subtracts the floor.

title: Real homology, or length in disguise
text: And this is the failure the harness exists to catch. Two protein families separate cleanly on screen. That can mean the representation found real homology, or it can mean the representation encoded sequence length, and length happens to differ between those families. In a scatter plot, those two look identical. The confound group added this week refuses to let them.

title: Sixty-one statements that left the report
text: Then the same release caught its own instrument. Coverage had been told to ignore any line that is just an ellipsis, the abstract method placeholder. The pattern was never anchored, so it also matched a type annotation tuple of string ellipsis, and coverage discards the entire statement a matching line belongs to. 61 statements quietly left the report. 47 of them sat in the module that scores everything else.

title: Abort the matrix, or isolate the pair
text: Breadth also changes what a single bug costs. NMF refuses signed input. A manifold method can fail on a disconnected neighbor graph. At four pairs, those are exceptions. Across a full matrix, they are ordinary. Previously, any one of them discarded every pair that had already succeeded. That was the fork this week actually turned on.

title: Verdict — the defences are the release
text: So, two releases, one week. The breadth is the headline. The defenses are the release. And the coverage bug is the part worth keeping because it is the same mistake the whole tool exists to find. A number that looked fine while quietly measuring less than it claimed.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn, and you can run this against anything you are about to publish. Here is a benchmark result. Before you tell me whether the score is good, tell me what a random control would have scored on the same data, what the result becomes if the representation encodes only length, and whether the tooling I used to check my own work is itself being checked. Then tell me which one I forgot.

title: Outro
text: What the measure was hiding. Sigh.
